title: Thick Italian hot chocolate
intro: Spoon-thick like an Italian café's, with real dark chocolate and a little starch.

steps.t: Finely chop the dark chocolate.
In a small pan, stir together the cocoa, sugar and cornstarch, crushing any lumps.
Pour in the cold milk slowly, whisking until smooth.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring, then simmer for 3 minutes, until it coats the spoon.
steps.label: Thicken

steps.t: Take off the heat, add the chocolate and salt and stir until glossy and smooth.
Pour into cups and serve right away; it thickens further as it cools.

tips.t: A pinch of cinnamon and one of chilli give it a Mexican twist.
Serve with whipped cream and ladyfingers for dunking.
Leftovers set in the fridge: eat it cold like a pudding.

title: Masala chai latte
intro: Black tea boiled with whole spices and milk, the way it's made in India.

steps.t: Crush the cardamom and peppercorns with the base of a glass and slice the ginger.
Put the water, spices and ginger in a small pan, bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Spices

steps.t: Add the tea and sugar and boil for 2 minutes, until the liquid is dark mahogany.
steps.label: Tea

steps.t: Pour in the milk and bring back to a boil; when it froths up, lower the heat and cook 2 more minutes.
steps.label: Milk

steps.t: Strain into cups through a fine sieve and serve piping hot.

tips.t: Pour the chai between two pans from a height, like a chaiwala: it turns frothy.
Half a star anise or a few fennel seeds change the chai's character.
Oat milk makes it vegan: add it last and heat without boiling.

title: Golden milk
intro: Warm almond milk with turmeric, ginger and cinnamon, mellow and spiced.

steps.t: In a small pan, whisk the turmeric, cinnamon and pepper with a little almond milk into a smooth paste.
Add the rest of the almond milk, the ginger and the coconut oil.
Heat gently for 5 minutes, stirring: it should steam and barely simmer, not boil hard.
steps.label: Infuse

steps.t: Take off the heat, sweeten with the maple syrup and strain into cups.
For a froth, buzz it for a few seconds with a stick blender or milk frother.

tips.t: You won't taste the black pepper, but it rounds out the turmeric: don't skip it.
Whole cow's milk makes it creamier, though no longer vegan.

title: Moka pot coffee done right
intro: Three moves make the difference: hot water, loose grounds, low flame.

steps.t: Fill the base with already hot water up to just below the valve, never above it.
Fit the funnel and fill it with coffee in a slight mound without tamping; level with a finger.
Wipe any grounds off the rim and screw the top on firmly, holding the hot base with a cloth.
Set over medium-low heat with the lid open; the flame must not reach past the base.
When the coffee, dark at first, turns pale and starts to gurgle, take it off the heat at once.
Close the lid, stir the coffee in the pot with a teaspoon and pour into small cups.

tips.t: Off the heat, run the base under cold water to stop bitter, burnt notes.
Leftover cold coffee is perfect for an Espresso Martini.
Never wash the moka pot with soap: hot water only, and let it dry open.

title: Mulled wine (vin brulé)
intro: Red wine warmed gently with orange and spices, as at Alpine Christmas markets.

steps.t: Wash the orange, slice one half and juice the other.
In a stainless pan, combine the wine, sugar, orange juice and slices, lemon peel and spices.
Warm over low heat, stirring, until the sugar dissolves; don't let it boil.
Keep it on the lowest heat for 15 minutes: it should just steam (about 70 °C), not simmer.
steps.label: Infuse

steps.t: Turn off the heat, cover and leave to rest for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Strain and serve hot in mugs or heatproof glasses, with an orange slice.

tips.t: Never let it boil: the alcohol evaporates and the spices turn bitter.
Alcohol-free: use red grape juice and cut the sugar to 20 g.
Serve with roast chestnuts or spiced biscuits.
